paper_title: Counting Permutation Patterns with Multidimensional Trees
classifications: Mathematics of computing → Permutations and combinations
statement: 1. Maximum size versus rank. For a given integer s, denote by f (s) the largest integer k such that the subspace spanned by the vectors of pattern-trees over at most k points, of maximum size s and with no equalities, is of full dimension, |S≤k |. The results of [18] imply that f (1) = 3. In Section 3.3 and Section 3.4 we prove f (2) = 7, and in Section 3.5 we show that f (s) ≥ 2s, for every s ≥ 1. What is the behavior of f (s)? For example, do we have f (s) ≥ 4s ± o(s), as attained by the technique of [7]? 2. A fine-grained variant of f (s). For integers s and k, let g(s, k) be the number of linearly independent vectors in QSk generated by Algorithm 1 when applied to trees of maximum size s over k permutation points with no equalities. What is the general behavior of g(s, k)? This generalises a question of [18] about corner-trees. The following values are presently known.

statement: 3. Complexity of k-profile, for 5 ≤ k ≤ 7. Can the time complexity for finding the 5, 6, 7-profiles be improved further, perhaps by utilising techniques along the lines of Section 4? In particular, we ask whether the 6-profile can be computed in sub-quadratic time. 4. Study of the 8-profile. [15] shows the equivalence between the computation of the 4-profile and counting 4-cycles in sparse graphs. In Section 3.4 we show that many of the observations of [15] can be extended to S8 . In fact, we conjecture that there exists an analogous hardness result for k = 8, and we refer the reader to Section 3.4 where the details are discussed.
